The exercises here use the 1,797 handwritten digits that the course overview loads
from the [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/80) [@alpaydin1998optdigits],
from the same local copy, [`data/optdigits-test.csv`](data/optdigits-test.csv).
They also use two of its [features](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/course-overview.html#def-feature),
each an average of an 8 by 8 image's pixels,
with rows and columns counted from 0:

- [center ink](course-overview.qmd#sol-zero-or-one), over rows 2 to 5 and columns 3 and 4;
- [left ink](course-overview.qmd#sol-three-or-eight), over rows 2 to 5 and columns 0 to 2.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

digits = pd.read_csv("data/optdigits-test.csv", header=None)
pixels = digits.iloc[:, :64].to_numpy()
labels = digits[64].to_numpy()
images = pixels.reshape(-1, 8, 8)

center_ink = images[:, 2:6, 3:5].mean(axis=(1, 2))
left_ink = images[:, 2:6, 0:3].mean(axis=(1, 2))
print(images.shape, center_ink[:5], left_ink[:5])
```
